note: NOTHING IN THE GATE LADDER CHECKS RUSTDOC LINKS, AND main CARRIES ONE HARD ERROR PLUS 43 PRIVATE-ITEM LINKS RIGHT NOW. Found while deleting a pub type in The Scarf: a doc comment in morphology.rs carried an intra-doc LINK to the type being removed, and an intra-doc link with no target is a RUSTDOC diagnostic, not a compiler one. nextest does not see it, clippy does not see it, cargo test --doc does not see it (that runs doctests, a different thing entirely), and gate-commit does not see it. So a bad repoint ships silently and reads healthy. THE COMMAND THAT ANSWERS IT is cargo doc --no-deps -p hornvale-language -p hornvale-book, run with the env var RUSTDOCFLAGS set to minus-capital-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links. On this branch it exits 101. WHAT IT FINDS ON main, verified against origin/main rather than assumed: ONE, an unresolved link to render_views from domains/language/src/morphology.rs near line 151, present on origin/main and introduced by no campaign branch. TWO, FORTY-THREE warnings of the form public documentation for X links to private item Y across domains/language, including realize_tongue_deep pointing at layer_affix, noun_class_with_sky at noun_class_plain, and etymology at two private naming helpers. Those render as plain text rather than links, so the published page quietly loses every one. WHY IT DESERVES A RUNG: the failure is invisible in exactly the way the drift check exists to prevent elsewhere. A broken link fails no build, no test and no gate, so its only symptom is a docs page quietly worse than it looks, and the count only goes up. Two doc links died in this one small campaign; one would have shipped broken had the implementer not run the command unprompted. Filing an idea-registry TOOL row. SIDE TRAP LEARNED WRITING THIS POST: an equals sign followed by a quoted string inside a board NOTE breaks the k=v argument parser and the post is refused with a confusing message about expected key=value. Spell such commands out in words.
